tagline: A 2,500 km Indian Ocean coast of islands and estuaries — Maputo's bay, the Bazaruto archipelago, and crossings only the water can make.
summary: Mozambique stretches along 2,500 km of Indian Ocean coast strung with bays, estuaries and island archipelagos. The capital Maputo sits on a wide bay facing Catembe and the Inhaca and Portuguese islands; the Bazaruto archipelago off Vilankulo is a marquee marine-park resort cluster; and estuary towns like Inhambane–Maxixe and Beira–Buzi are separated by water that road cannot bridge. Many of these crossings are water-only, and the resort islands are reached by slow boats — a natural fit for a clean foiling tier on both commuter estuaries and luxury island hops.
why_marine_mobility: Mozambique's coast is defined by water gaps: bay crossings, estuary mouths and island archipelagos that road simply cannot serve. Navier's Pioneer II flies the bay and estuary hops — Maputo to Catembe and the Inhaca islands, Inhambane to Maxixe, the Bazaruto island runs — silent and zero-emission, while the Quanta-LR range opens longer coastal connections along the Indian Ocean shore. It is a market split between essential estuary crossings and high-value marine-park tourism.

demand_signals.label: Maputo Bay crossings
demand_signals.note: Maputo to Catembe (now bridged but congested) and to the Inhaca and Portuguese islands are bay crossings where water is the direct link from the capital.

demand_signals.label: Bazaruto archipelago
demand_signals.note: The Bazaruto, Benguerra and Magaruque islands off Vilankulo form a marquee marine-park resort cluster reached by boat — a high-spend, water-only luxury market.

demand_signals.label: Estuary towns
demand_signals.note: Inhambane–Maxixe and Beira–Buzi are separated by estuaries where the ferry is the everyday connection, today on slow conventional craft.

use_cases.body: Clean foiling bay and estuary crossings — Maputo to Catembe and the Inhaca islands, Inhambane to Maxixe — upgrading slow ferries on water-only connections.
Premium island transfers to the Bazaruto archipelago resorts off Vilankulo, replacing slow boat transfers with fast, dry, zero-emission hops.
Marine-park and coastal-leisure runs along the Indian Ocean shore, on low-wash craft suited to protected reef environments.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The bay, estuary and archipelago meshes — Maputo↔Catembe (~1.5 nm), Maputo↔Inhaca (~22 nm), Maputo↔Portuguese Island (~20 nm), Vilankulo↔Bazaruto (~16 nm), Inhambane↔Maxixe (~2.5 nm), Beira↔Buzi (~25 nm) — sit inside the 70 nm all-electric range on sheltered bays and estuaries.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The local crossings are Pioneer II territory; Quanta-LR hybrid range opens longer Indian Ocean coastal line-haul between the archipelagos and estuary towns without charging build-out along a sparsely served coast.

signature_routes.label: Maputo ↔ Catembe / Inhaca Island (all-electric bay crossing)

transit_planning: For Mozambique's maritime administration, the Bazaruto National Park authority or resort operators: a clean tier across essential estuary crossings and high-value marine-park island transfers, off existing piers and resort jetties.
competitive_landscape: Coastal and estuary transport relies on slow diesel ferries and traditional boats; the Bazaruto resorts run private island transfers. There is no fast, clean, premium foiling tier on either the commuter crossings or the luxury island runs, leaving greenfield room across both segments.
regulatory_note: Maritime activity falls under Mozambique's National Maritime Authority (INAMAR) and port administrations, with the Bazaruto Archipelago National Park imposing conservation rules that favour zero-emission, low-wash craft. The marine-park status makes Navier's clean profile a regulatory advantage on the luxury island routes.
seasonality: A tropical climate with a wet, cyclone-prone summer (November–April) and a calmer, drier winter (May–October) that is the peak for the Bazaruto resorts and reliable estuary operation; the bay and estuary crossings run year-round on sheltered water, while coastal line-haul favours the calmer season.
